content: Horizontal transmission refers to the spread of bacterial, fungal, or viral infections between individuals of the same species who are not in a parent-child relationship. There are two primary mechanisms of horizontal transmission: anterior station and posterior station. In anterior station transmission, the infection is transmitted through the bite of an infected organism. Examples of diseases transmitted in this manner include malaria, dengue fever, and bubonic plague. Posterior station transmission occurs through contact with infected fecal material. For instance, diseases caused by rickettsiae, such as typhus, are contracted when the fecal matter of a body louse is scratched into the bloodstream. Horizontal transmission is often associated with the evolution of virulence in pathogens. As such, it is a concept of significant importance in the field of evolutionary medicine.
